scope: Proposition 4.5 (Uniform comparison at the targets) of the manuscript “A Codimension-One Bound for the Singular Set of a Stationary Integral Varifold” (preprints/A-Codimension-One-Bound-for-the-Singular-Set-of-a-Stationary-Integral-Varifold-October-5-2026/varifold-singular-dimension.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 346 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 550b6c1b4bf40bda), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: All sufficiently late Li belong to intervals (4.23). After passing to a subsequence, either one interval extends to zero and contains all these targets, or the indices of their covering intervals tend to infinity. In the latter case, on each sufficiently late covering interval, |P(r)| ≤ C (B∗b ≤ r ≤ r∗), (4.24) and (4.21) holds there with uniform constants. In the former case the same conclusions hold on the sufficiently small-radius part of the fixed interval.
